searchProcedure.implementation: fit/search.py, fit/fit.py (W47's, inherited by path and pinned by part 1)
searchProcedure.text: W45's procedure: within a stage, its families are sequential components in familyOrder, each swept on the stage's scope from the point the previous left; within a family each leaf's grid is swept in the order listed, the others held at their current values, at most two passes; a factorialGroups entry sweeps its keys' grid product as ONE coordinate step; a grid point outside a declared joint domain (domainLowerIsMinus) is not a candidate; every step's candidates include the step's start (already measured), so a sweep never forces a move off the incumbent.
searchProcedure.tieRule: points whose objective lies within the stage tie of the step's minimum are indistinguishable; among them the point nearest the step's start wins (the sum over the step's keys of |v - v0| / (domain hi - lo)), then fewer moved leaves, then grid order; the stage decision applies the same rule measured from the stage base. The tie is rule.stage_tie computed once on the stage's declared cells from the reference's own cut (stage 1 0.0365, stage 2 0.0544), never from a point's partial render (the W44 and W45 tracker entries).
searchProcedure.objective: rule.stage_objective: W44's selection metric (median |log(web/native)| over F, C and P) on the stage's cells, both dark scales pooled, the gate partition; a partial objective is never ranked (recover.py, or refusal)
searchProcedure.scaleSeparableRendering: a point's render at one scale is its scale twin's: the point's overrides restricted to the leaves acting at that scale (fit/labels.json `scales`); points whose scale twins have equal resolved digests share that scale's render. Exact under the scale anchoring, which ladders (ii) and (iii) read on every lever (its other scale byte-identical to the control's).
searchProcedure.renders: every fit render in candidate mode on the WebGPU tier with --alpha, through with-gpu.sh; each scope's cells are the dark T1 gate cells of its pose plus L1's declared population of that pose

selectionRule.withinAStage: the stage's point with a passing within clause (rule.stage_within: every target cell of the stage within) and the smallest stage objective lands
selectionRule.ifNotWithin: else the smallest stage objective, an indistinguishable plateau decided by the tie rule from the stage base; recorded as NOT within

postGateSelection.rule: Inside the objective's declared tie of a stage's minimum, over every rendered point of that stage, the point with the fewest cells away beyond B summed over both scales is selected, then the fewest past 3 B, then the hashed tie rule. The budget of a rendered point is read by its exact composite (its own rest cells with the landed inactive cells, the receded document unchanged). This is a post-hoc selection among measured points, made after the gate, and the record says so; the selected point is re-rendered in full at the freeze and its gate reading must agree with the composite within the run-to-run bar.
postGateSelection.stage2Composite: a stage-2 point's composite is its own inactive cells with the selected stage-1 point's rest cells
postGateSelection.ruling: W48 Decision Log 9 and its addendum (the user's ship ruling, tie-broken by the budget; the parent's option 1)
postGateSelection.madeAfter: the fit (part 2 ad5fdeceb244 as hashed) and the gate on its landed point (G1 head c85ba1ada)
postGateSelection.implementation: packages/calibration/results/2026-10-06-w48-g1-refit/fit/select_dl9.py (budget by reselect.py, the landing rule's rule.evaluate); path/d0219/dl9-selection.json
